title: Veridian Manufacturing — Edge VPC + Terraform Modules Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose / audience:
This is a working playbook for the Veridian Manufacturing edge/private deployment. Audience: platform engineer (Veridian), solutions engineer (Redwood), SRE assigned to the customer.

Summary (one-liner):
Deploy Redwood Private into Veridian’s on-prem edge cluster (three-site setup) using our Terraform modules with explicit network segmentation and staged upgrade path to minimize downtime and rollback risk.

High-level constraints / customer context:
- Customer: Veridian Manufacturing (factory floor compute at 3 regional plants: MN-plant, TX-plant, OH-plant).
- No public egress for inference traffic; control-plane egress permitted to redwood-control.redwood.ai:443 through a pinned NAT gateway.
- Existing on-prem k8s distribution: Rancher-managed RKE2 (v1.27.5).
- Hardware available at edge: 2x A100 (80GB) per rack (expected to dedicate 1 GPU per node for initial tenant), 192GB RAM, local NVMe 4TB.
- Network: 10Gb internal fabric, separate VLANs available per plant.
- Security: customer uses HashiCorp Vault + HSM for KMS integration; Redwood must support customer-managed keys.

Target SLOs and non-functional requirements:
- 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms for 2k prompt length on small-gen models (quantized FP16 variants).
- Inference throughput target: 2500 tokens/sec per plant steady state during day shift; burst to 5k tokens/sec for 10 minutes.
- RTO for control-plane changes: 15 minutes.
- Patch/upgrade window: 2am–4am local plant time, rolling across plants.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Customer will reserve 1 A100 per plant node for Redwood workloads initially; additional GPUs can be added if utilization > 70%.
- Persistent model artifacts will be stored on local NVMe and replicated to a central S3-compatible object store (MinIO) nightly.
- KV cache persistence is ephemeral and rebuilt on restart; accepting ~1–2 second cold start penalty for first token generation after full restart.
- Customer provides IP allowlist for control-plane egress and an internal DNS entry for their private registry (registry.veridian.local).

Recommended architecture (concise):
- Control plane (Redwood-managed): a lightweight control-plane agent runs in customer VPC (control-plane proxy) that talks back to Redwood control-plane over TLS. No persistent customer data sent to hosted control plane except telemetry/metrics; model artifacts and user data remain in customer network.
- Data plane: inference runtime runs inside customer k8s cluster, deployed as a DaemonSet across GPU nodes with nodeSelectors for GPU instance type. Model shards loaded from local NVMe.
- Networking: Create three micro-VLANs per plant: management (agents, control-plane), inference (runtime pods), and storage (MinIO, NFS). Use strict NetworkPolicy to limit pod egress.

Terraform module notes (practical/work-in-progress):
- Modules to use: redwood-private/vpc, redwood-private/k8s-roles, redwood-private/gpu-nodepool, redwood-private/minio-helm.
- Known gaps: our redwood-private/gpu-nodepool module assumes cloud provider node lifecycle APIs; for RKE2 we use a thin shim module (rke2-nodepool-shim) that translates the same inputs (node_count, gpu_type, taints) into provisioning steps via customer-provided automation.
- Inputs we will set in Veridian vars: gpu_type=A100-80, node_count=3 (one per plant to start), nvme_size_gb=4000, taints=["redwood=inference:NoSchedule"], k8s_version=1.27.5.
- Important variables: model_cache_path (absolute path on host), local_registry (registry.veridian.local:5000), kms_key_id (Vault path).
- Outputs to wire: kubeconfig_path, node_ips (list), minio_endpoint, control_agent_tls_cert_id.
- Terraform state: store backend in customer S3-compatible endpoint (MinIO) with server-side encryption; remote locking via Dynamo-compatible service (etcd lock shim) — implementation doc in linked_artifacts.

Practical terraform quirks we encountered and workarounds: 
- RKE2 nodepool lifecycle: shim must call customer Ansible playbooks to set GPU drivers because driver install cannot be reliably done in a cloud-init style environment. Documented Ansible playbook: drive://shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/ansible-rke2-gpu-install.yaml
- TLS certs: control-agent cert rotation uses Vault PKI; our module expects certs in PEM files — include a small helper script (vault-pki-export.sh) in repo.
- Module versioning: pin redwood-private modules to v0.13.x for this customer due to API stability.

Sizing rationale and numbers (initial):
- Model family: base quantized transformer (~20B quantized to 16-bit-INT8 path). Expected tokens/sec per A100-80: ~280 tokens/sec for generation-only with batch 1, ~900 tokens/sec with dynamic batching.
- To meet 2500 tokens/sec steady state: 3 nodes with one A100 each with batching enabled (autoscaler target avg 250 tokens/sec per GPU). Keep headroom for spikes -> recommended initial capacity = 4 GPUs across cluster (deploy 3 active, 1 hot spare/burst pool).
- RAM sizing: runtime container needs 64GB reserved; host 192GB sufficient for model residency and kube overhead.
- Disk: model cache (NVMe) requirement per node = 2TB usable (for hosting multiple model versions). Use 4TB physical, zfs/raid-0 not required.

Upgrade plan (major release example: runtime 2.1.0 -> 3.0.0):
- Goals: zero user-impact for in-flight requests; graceful fallback to previous stable model/runtime if regression.
- Stages:
  1) Preflight (run E2E tests in CI using customer-provided sample prompts and metrics). Confirm performance within 10% of baseline.
  2) Canary on spare GPU node in MN-plant: deploy runtime 3.0.0 with limited traffic (5%). Run A/B evaluation against baseline model for quality regressions.
  3) Gradual rollout across inference nodes (30% -> 60% -> 100%) per plant, wait 30 minutes between steps while monitoring latency, error rate, and quality deltas.
  4) Post-rollout smoke test and revert window (2 hours) with automated rollback job that can re-apply terraform to restore previous runtime image.
- Rollback plan: terraform apply with pinned runtime_image and restart daemonset with zero-downtime draining strategy. For model compatibility breaks, fallback policy will route requests to base model variant until full migration.

Operational checklists (for SRE/SE during deploy):
- Pre-deploy: verify vault access, kubeconfig, node GPU driver status, local_registry reachable, minio endpoints accessible.
- During canary: monitor token latency P50/P95, batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization.
- Post-deploy: validate telemetry ingestion, trace context propagation, per-route cost metrics, confirm billing tags assigned.

Architecture Q&A (anticipated customer questions & answers):
- Q: Does Redwood store customer inference data off-site?
  A: No. Only ephemeral telemetry and anonymized health metrics are optionally sent. Model artifacts and user queries remain in customer network unless they explicitly opt in.
- Q: How do we rotate KMS keys?
  A: We support Vault/HSM-driven rotation. Key IDs are passed to the terraform module; rotation is coordinated via a scheduled job that updates control-agent certs and re-encrypts object store secrets.
- Q: What happens if a plant loses network connectivity to control plane?
  A: Data plane continues serving for a configurable grace period (72 hours) with local metrics buffering. During this time, model updates and control-plane driven rollouts will be paused.

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- Confirm whether Veridian will accept a single NAT egress IP per plant or prefer a CIDR range (owner: Veridian netops).
- Add support for Ceph/Rook as alternative to MinIO if customer wants block-level replication (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Validate Ansible GPU driver playbook on Veridian hardware (task: run on staging rack).
- Add formal runbook for full data-plane recovery after complete power loss (owner: Evelyn Chen).

Risk matrix (short):
- Biggest risk: driver/OS incompatibilities on older firmware -> mitigations: staged driver testing on spare nodes, hardware firmware checklist.
- Security risk: misconfigured network policies -> mitigation: automated NetworkPolicy linting preflight.
- Cost risk: model residency overflows NVMe -> mitigation: enforce LRU eviction and size quotas.

Next steps / immediate plan (1–3 weeks):
1) Align on NAT egress IP format and confirm firewall rules (owner: Veridian netops / Aisha).
2) Run terraform plan with shim in staging and validate outputs (owner: Samir).
3) Execute a smoke deploy on MN-plant spare node, run A/B tests (owner: Marco).
4) Document rollback runbook in Confluence and link from terraform repo (owner: Aisha).

Appendix: useful commands / snippets
- terraform: terraform init -backend-config="bucket=veridian-terraform-state" -var-file=veridian.tfvars
- ansible: ansible-playbook -i inventory/rke2-plant-mn playbooks/gpu-install.yaml
- verify GPUs: kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu}'

Notes: This document is intentionally informal — contains checklist items, questions to validate with Veridian product/security teams, and terraform pragmatics that will be refined into the module README when we converge.
